extendedData.magicalUses: Used chiefly to complete Centaurus's sprawling outline.

entities.description: Fawaris, 'the riders,' marks one wing of the Swan alongside Sadr, extending the Northern Cross figure outward. Its name is thought to recall a group of horsemen from older Arabic star-lore rather than anything specific to the swan-myth.

extendedData.magicalUses: Used to complete the Cross's western arm; little individual lore attaches beyond the constellation's general character.

entities.description: Zeta Cygni, without a widely used proper name, extends the Swan's tail region beyond Deneb, one of the fainter points needed to round out Cygnus's full cross-and-wingspan outline.

extendedData.planetaryNature: Nature of Venus, by its warm yellow-white hue
extendedData.magicalUses: Used chiefly to complete the Swan's outline.

entities.description: Edasich, 'the hyena,' marks a point along Draco's long, winding body between the head and the coils that pass near the two Bears. It was notable to modern astronomers as the first star beyond the solar system where a planet was suspected from radial-velocity measurements.

extendedData.magicalUses: Used for patient, hidden discovery — fitting for a star later linked to one of the first exoplanet detections.

entities.description: Aldhibah, 'the hyenas,' continues Draco's winding path further along the coil, sharing the constellation's watchful, coiled character.

extendedData.magicalUses: Used to extend the coiled, watchful quality of the Dragon's body along its long path.

entities.description: Altais, 'the goats,' marks a further bend in Draco's long body as it winds toward Ursa Minor. Its gentler Saturn-Venus temperament softens the more aggressive character read into the Dragon's head-stars.

extendedData.magicalUses: Used for endurance softened by grace, continuing the long, patient coil of the Dragon.

entities.description: Athebyne marks a further point on Draco's coil, one of the constellation's brighter mid-body stars linking the head region to the stars that curl between the Great and Little Bears.

extendedData.magicalUses: Used to extend the coiled, watchful quality of the Dragon's body along its long path.

entities.description: Beid, 'the egg,' marks an early bend in the River not far from its source near Orion's foot, one of a pair of neighbouring stars — Beid and Keid — historically associated with the eggs of an ostrich in older Arabic star-lore.

extendedData.magicalUses: Used for the beginning stages of a long undertaking, fitting the egg-imagery of its name.

entities.description: Keid, Beid's neighbouring 'egg' star, is notable to modern astronomy as one of the nearest Sun-like stars with a known planetary system, orbited by a white dwarf and a red dwarf companion as well.

extendedData.magicalUses: Used, like Beid, for the early stages of long undertakings and the eggs from which they hatch.

entities.description: Rana, 'the frog,' marks a further bend along the River's winding southward course, continuing Eridanus's long path toward Achernar.

extendedData.magicalUses: Used chiefly to complete the River's long winding outline.

entities.description: Azha, 'the ostrich nest,' continues the same older Arabic imagery as Beid and Keid, marking another bend of the River as it winds south.

extendedData.magicalUses: Used chiefly to complete the River's long winding outline.

entities.description: Mebsuta, 'the outstretched paw' (or, in some readings, 'the lion's forearm' from an older figure once mapped onto this region), marks one of the Twins' arms or shoulders, extending Castor's figure downward.

extendedData.magicalUses: Used for a reaching, outstretched gesture — extending toward something just beyond grasp.

entities.description: Propus, 'the forward foot,' marks the leading foot of the Twins figure, a red variable star whose brightness shifts noticeably over roughly eight months.

extendedData.magicalUses: Used for forward motion and the first step of a shared undertaking.

entities.description: Kajam, of disputed but likely Arabic origin referring to a stalk or spike, marks one of the fainter points along Hercules's outstretched limbs, needed to complete the kneeling hero's full, sprawling figure.

extendedData.magicalUses: Used mainly to complete the Kneeler's outline; little distinct lore attaches to it.

entities.description: Marsic, 'the elbow,' marks a joint along Hercules's raised arm, one of the fainter stars filling out the hero's sprawling, kneeling figure between the keystone and his weapon-bearing hand.

extendedData.magicalUses: Used mainly to complete the hero's outline; little distinct lore attaches to it.

entities.description: Maasym, 'the wrist,' continues the arm begun at Marsic's elbow, another modest star needed to complete Hercules's full figure.

extendedData.magicalUses: Used mainly to complete the hero's outline; little distinct lore attaches to it.

entities.description: Ukdah, 'the knot,' marks a bend well along Hydra's immense winding body, past Alphard's isolated brilliance and toward the serpent's tail beneath Libra and Centaurus.

extendedData.magicalUses: Used for the knots and turning-points along a very long undertaking.

entities.description: Zeta Hydrae, without a widely used proper name, marks an early bend of the Water Serpent's body not far past its head, one of the many points needed to trace out the longest of all constellations.

extendedData.planetaryNature: Nature of Jupiter, by its warm golden-orange hue
extendedData.magicalUses: Used chiefly to complete Hydra's exceptionally long winding outline.

entities.description: Xi Hydrae continues the Serpent's body further along its great length, one of a chain of similarly modest stars that give Hydra its distinctively drawn-out shape.

extendedData.planetaryNature: Nature of Jupiter, by its warm golden-orange hue
extendedData.magicalUses: Used chiefly to complete Hydra's exceptionally long winding outline.

entities.description: Beta Hydrae marks a point well along the Serpent's tail, one of the final stars needed to trace Hydra's body all the way to its tip beneath Centaurus and Libra.

extendedData.magicalUses: Used chiefly to complete Hydra's exceptionally long winding outline.

entities.description: Adhafera, 'the curl,' marks a point in the Lion's mane within the sickle asterism, between Algieba and the sickle's topmost star. Its name refers to the curling tuft of the mane it traces.

extendedData.magicalUses: Used for refinement and careful attention to detail, fitting the delicate curl its name describes.

entities.description: Zubenelhakrabi, 'the scorpion's claw,' preserves most directly of all Libra's stars the constellation's older identity as the claws of the neighbouring Scorpion, before Roman astronomers carved the Scales out as their own figure.

extendedData.magicalUses: Used as a reminder of what lies beneath an apparently balanced surface — the claw within the scale.

entities.description: Zeta Lyrae, without a widely used proper name, marks the fourth corner of the small parallelogram beneath Vega, completing Lyra's compact and easily traced shape.

extendedData.planetaryNature: Nature of Venus, by its clear white hue
extendedData.magicalUses: Used chiefly to complete the Lyre's small, well-defined outline.

entities.description: Yed Prior, 'the preceding hand,' marks one of the serpent-charmer's hands as he grips Serpens, paired with Yed Posterior just beside it. Together the two 'hand' stars are among the most easily recognised pairs in Ophiuchus.

extendedData.magicalUses: Used for the grip and grasp needed to master something dangerous but valuable, echoing the hand that holds the serpent.

entities.description: Yed Posterior, 'the following hand,' completes the close pair with Yed Prior marking Ophiuchus's grip on the serpent. The two stars sit close enough together to be distinguished with the naked eye as a wide, easy double.

extendedData.magicalUses: Used alongside Yed Prior for the grip and grasp needed to master something dangerous but valuable.

entities.description: Biham, from an Arabic term for young horses, marks a point along Pegasus's neck, extending the constellation's outline beyond the Great Square toward Enif at the muzzle.

extendedData.magicalUses: Used for youthful energy and the eagerness of a horse not yet fully broken.

entities.description: Homam, 'the man of great spirit,' continues the line from Biham toward Enif, filling out the winged horse's neck and head region beyond the four corners of the Great Square.

extendedData.magicalUses: Used for spirited resolve carried through a long undertaking.

entities.description: Epsilon Piscis Austrini, without a widely used proper name, marks a point along the small loop of stars forming the Southern Fish's body, filling out the circlet around bright Fomalhaut.

extendedData.planetaryNature: Nature of Venus, by its clear white hue
extendedData.magicalUses: Used chiefly to complete the Southern Fish's outline.

entities.description: Sargas marks a bright point along the Scorpion's curling tail, one of the ancient names for this region reaching back to Babylonian star-lists that treated Scorpius as sacred to the underworld. Its Jupiter-Saturn nature was read as slow, weighty fortune, earned through the tail's long curling patience.

extendedData.magicalUses: Used for fortune that accumulates slowly and is earned through patient endurance.

entities.description: Alniyat, 'the arteries,' marks a point close by Antares, one of two stars historically sharing this name (the other being Tau Scorpii on Antares's other side) — the pair flanking the Scorpion's fiery heart like the great vessels of a body.

extendedData.magicalUses: Used for the vital, life-carrying energy that flows close beside a powerful centre.

entities.description: Jabbah, 'the forehead,' marks a point in the Scorpion's head and claws region near Dschubba and Graffias, a multiple-star system that appears single to the naked eye.

extendedData.magicalUses: Used to complete the Scorpion's head region alongside Dschubba and Graffias.

entities.description: Mu Serpentis, without a widely used proper name, marks a point in Serpens Caput between Unukalhai's neck and the tail-half of the constellation across Ophiuchus.

extendedData.magicalUses: Used chiefly to complete the Serpent's outline.

entities.description: Beta Serpentis marks a point in the head region of Serpens Caput, close by the small triangle of stars that frame Unukalhai's neck.

extendedData.magicalUses: Used chiefly to complete the Serpent's outline.

entities.description: Heze marks a point on Virgo's outstretched wing near Porrima, of uncertain but likely Arabic origin, extending the Maiden's sprawling figure across a wide stretch of sky.

extendedData.magicalUses: Used to extend the Maiden's outstretched, harvest-bearing gesture.

entities.description: Auva marks a point closer to Virgo's body between the wings and the wheat-sheaf hand holding Spica, filling in the wide central span of the constellation's figure.

extendedData.magicalUses: Used mainly to complete the Maiden's central span; little distinct lore attaches to it.

entities.description: Syrma, 'the train' (of a garment), marks the trailing hem of the Maiden's robe, one of the southernmost points completing Virgo's very large figure.

extendedData.magicalUses: Used for what trails behind and completes a larger, more prominent whole.

entities.description: Deneb el Okab, 'the eagle's tail,' marks the Eagle's tail feathers opposite Altair at the bird's head, completing Aquila's outline as a bird in full flight.

extendedData.magicalUses: Used for the trailing, steadying feathers that give flight its balance.

entities.description: Sadachbia, 'luck of the hidden things' or 'luck of the tents,' marks the near corner of the small Water Jar asterism within Aquarius, the cluster of four modest stars representing the jar itself rather than the Water-Bearer's body.

extendedData.magicalUses: Traditionally read as bringing good fortune to what is hidden or stored away, fitting a star marking the vessel itself.

entities.description: Albali, 'the swallower,' marks a point on the Water-Bearer's arm as he pours the stream downward toward Piscis Austrinus. Its name recalls the star's old association with drought and the swallowing-up of water rather than its release.

extendedData.magicalUses: Used with some caution in workings involving the withholding rather than the giving of resources.

entities.description: Ancha, 'the hip,' marks the Water-Bearer's hip on the figure's far side from the jar and stream, filling out Aquarius's full standing form.

extendedData.magicalUses: Used mainly to complete the Water-Bearer's outline; little distinct lore attaches to it.

entities.description: Sadaltager, 'luck of the merchant,' marks another corner of the small Water Jar asterism alongside Sadachbia, a close binary star that together with its neighbours traces the jar's compact outline.

extendedData.magicalUses: Traditionally read as favourable for trade and commerce, in keeping with its name.

entities.description: Seat, of disputed origin, completes the small Water Jar cluster within Aquarius, the faintest of the four stars marking the vessel from which the constellation's stream pours.

extendedData.magicalUses: Used mainly to complete the Water Jar asterism; little distinct lore attaches to it.
